reason: H0 fuzzes JSON decoding through wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson, but it never directly constructs or operates on wuffs_aux::sync_io::DynIOBuffer. The changed allocation lifecycle—realloc(m_buf.data.ptr, n), unconditional free in drop and the destructor, and reuse after drop—is therefore not explicitly exercised across stateful call sequences or boundary-sized min_incl/max_incl values.
evidence: DynIOBuffer::grow changed from a malloc-versus-realloc branch guarded by allocated() to unconditional realloc(m_buf.data.ptr, static_cast<size_t>(n)).
DynIOBuffer::drop and DynIOBuffer::~DynIOBuffer changed to unconditional free(m_buf.data.ptr), and allocated() was removed.
The DynIOBuffer contract explicitly says that drop resets m_buf and that the object can be used after drop, creating a stateful grow/drop/grow/destruct protocol.

H0 directly invokes wuffs_json__decoder__initialize, wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens, and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson with wuffs_aux::sync_io::MemoryInput; no H0 identifier constructs DynIOBuffer or calls its grow or drop methods.
recommended_action: Add a dedicated DynIOBuffer fuzz target that derives max_incl, min_incl, and operation sequences from fuzz input; exercise construction, repeated grow calls, boundary and exceeding sizes, drop followed by regrowth, repeated drop, and destruction under memory sanitizers while checking GrowResult and m_buf size/index invariants.
